description: Idaho-only rules checked against the cited statutes and official DMV pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Where no special hazard requires a lower speed, Idaho's maximum in a residential, business, or urban district is
questions.explanation: Idaho Code 49-654(2)(a)(i) sets 35 miles per hour in any residential, business, or urban district unless otherwise posted under section 49-207(2) or (3).

questions.q: Idaho's maximum on an interstate highway is
options: 75 mph unless posted; 80 only after a study
80 mph on every interstate without a study
questions.explanation: Section 49-654(2)(a)(ii) sets 75 miles per hour on interstate highways unless otherwise posted under section 49-201(4), and allows 80 only if the department completes an engineering and traffic study, concludes the increase is in the public interest, and the transportation board concurs.

questions.q: Idaho's maximum on a state highway is
questions.explanation: Section 49-654(2)(a)(iii) sets 65 miles per hour on state highways unless otherwise posted under section 49-201(4), with a possible increase to 70 after an engineering and traffic study and Transportation Board concurrence.

questions.q: In other Idaho locations, the maximum is
questions.explanation: Section 49-654(2)(a)(iv) sets 55 miles per hour in other locations unless otherwise posted, up to a maximum of 70 miles per hour.

questions.q: In a posted Idaho school zone, a driver shall not exceed
options: A statewide 15 mph whenever a sign is present
A statewide 25 mph during school hours
The posted maximum speed limit for that school zone
35 mph, the urban maximum, even if a lower school speed is posted
questions.explanation: Section 49-658 says no person shall operate a vehicle in excess of the posted maximum speed limit established for a posted school zone. If the sign says "when children are present," that means one or more children on the same side of the street as the school building, or across the street, in any direction within the marked school zone.

questions.q: A person under 21 in Idaho is covered by a separate alcohol-driving offense at a concentration of
options: Any alcohol, including a zero reading
questions.explanation: Section 18-8004(1)(d) makes it unlawful for a person under twenty-one who has an alcohol concentration of at least 0.02 but less than 0.08 to drive or be in actual physical control. Penalties for that subsection are in section 18-8004A.

questions.q: An approved Idaho defensive-driving course may reduce the point total by
questions.explanation: The ITD guide says that once every three years a driver may reduce the point total by three points by completing an approved defensive driving course. Completion does not remove convictions, and it has no effect on a CDL disqualification. A driver may use only one such reduction in a three-year period, whether from a defensive-driving course or a traffic-safety course.

questions.q: Idaho may issue a driver-training instruction permit at age
questions.explanation: Section 49-307 and the ITD young-driver page provide driver-training and supervised-instruction permits at 14 1/2. A Class D license may not be issued sooner than age 15 and no sooner than six months after the permittee completes an approved driver-training course. 14 and one-half.

questions.q: During Idaho's supervised-instruction period, the permittee must accumulate
options: 50 hours over six months, 10 in darkness
40 hours, including 10 in bad weather only
questions.explanation: Section 49-307 requires at least 50 hours of supervised driving over a period of not less than six months, 10 hours of which shall be during hours of darkness. The supervising driver must be at least 21, hold a valid license, and occupy the seat beside the permittee. Those two are the only occupants of the front passenger section.

questions.q: An Idaho driver under 16 who has a valid license may drive
options: Only in daylight, or with a licensed adult 21+
Only with a parent, with no daylight rule
questions.explanation: The Idaho Transportation Department young-driver page states that daylight-only limit and the front-seat accompaniment exception for a driver under 16. Only during daylight, unless accompanied by a licensed person 21 or older sitting in the front seat.

questions.q: An approved Idaho driver-training program for an applicant under 17 includes
options: 50 hours of classroom and no car time
questions.explanation: The ITD young-driver page says an applicant under 17 must pass driver training, and an approved program consists of 30 hours of classroom instruction, six hours of in-car observation, and six hours of behind-the-wheel driving with an instructor. During class, a student at least 14 1/2 may drive only with the instructor.

questions.q: In Idaho, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Idaho requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Idaho complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Idaho requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Idaho teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Idaho requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Idaho: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

questions.q: In Idaho, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Idaho, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 15 years.

questions.q: In Idaho, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Idaho drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 16 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Idaho car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Idaho car knowledge test has 40 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Idaho car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 85% to pass the Idaho car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Idaho, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Idaho, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Idaho, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

questions.q: In Idaho, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Idaho brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Idaho, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Idaho residential district?
questions.explanation: Idaho sets 35 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Idaho?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Idaho can be posted up to 80 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Idaho rural interstate: up to 80 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Idaho's law on drivers using a phone?
options: No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
questions.explanation: Idaho: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Idaho?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Idaho, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: from a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Idaho left on red: onto a one-way street only.

questions.q: How is Idaho's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: Idaho seat belt enforcement is secondary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Idaho?
questions.explanation: Idaho requires a car seat or booster until 7 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Idaho: car or booster seat until 7 years.

questions.q: What is Idaho's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Idaho requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $15,000.

questions.q: Under Idaho's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Idaho can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 12 months.
